items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Yeah, I played trumpet with him.

ctx.x: I knew you made the records, but I didn't know you played trumpets with him.

Yeah, I played trumpet with him. That's where the woman liked to shot him down there one night. Really? Shot right through his coat and shirt right there. Well the blue singer, I forget her name. I'll tell you, her name was Ethel Cross. Ethel Cross. She was singing with me, she was a fool, you know. And they got to messing around with some other gal and they show them, she had a little automatic man. Shot right at him, shot right at home through there, that's who there. Another boy grabbed her, grabbed her hand.…

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: I made records with Jimmy Weed

ctx.x: He was on, he might have played bass on some of them records I made, I don't know, because I was with him right now. But I'll tell you the band, I made records with me and Al Wynn, then I made records with Francois Luzan, I made records with Jimmy Weed, I made records with Tiny Palm, then I made some of my own, you know, with a bunch I had. Somebody else I made records with, I can't think, no. I made records with a lot of guys.
I was just thinking about Tiny Palm, did you ever play any of his arrangements?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: The only guy that made records was Tiny Pong, Al Wynn, Jimmy Wade.

ctx.x: Nice piano player. When you played with Jelly Roll did you ever make any records with him? No, I didn't.

He didn't make no while I was with him. He had made some before I got with him. But I don't think he made no more after that. Because he died right after I got out of the band, me and Swayze. He didn't live long. But I heard all his records, Dr. Jazz and all that kind of stuff. But I didn't make any with him. He never made any records? The only guy that made records was Tiny Pong, Al Wynn, Jimmy Wade. He was a big chief. And what this guy named in New York, uh, the trombones. He's an Indian. Big chief. Oh, you…
Yeah, Bunk was there that year too. The Bunk sure was.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: I went and blew taps twice. I built a guy, Kelly, and another boy named Jimmy Wade.

ctx.x: Chicago? Well, they didn't do that there until they started getting all in and banged down there. The only thing I would play there on the streets was for the Elks' big convention. But I never played a funeral. And when people died there, I went and blew taps twice. I built a guy, Kelly, and another boy named Jimmy Wade. I didn't have a bang.
Just blew taps. Jimmy Wade the trumpet.
